summary: Lodestar Analytics — heartbeat storm induced priority inversion causing sustained request slowdown and invoiceable retry amplification
description:
Issue summary:
A rapid surge of internal heartbeat traffic from a misconfigured Lodestar edge agent caused a cascading priority inversion in the request scheduler. The scheduler demoted production inference requests behind大量 (large) internal control-heartbeat tasks, creating sustained tail latency increases and amplified client retries that were invoiceable.

Impact:
- Customer-facing completions for Lodestar experienced 3–7x P95/P99 latency for ~90 minutes (20:12 - 21:42 UTC).
- Streaming sessions intermittently cut off after heartbeat-driven connection churn.
- Billing exposure: automated retries from client SDKs resulted in ~12% billable token increase for affected window.
- Affected tenant: Lodestar Analytics (dedicated pool in us-east).

Environment:
- Production (dedicated capacity, us-east region)
- Serving runtime: tagged redwood-v1-release-2026-02
- Autoscaler: autoscaler-v2.4.1 with custom policy for Lodestar
- Edge agent: Lodestar-managed edge-agent v0.13.2 (misconfigured heartbeat interval)

Steps to reproduce (high confidence):
1) Deploy Lodestar edge-agent with heartbeat_interval=1s and control_queue=true in a test replica.
2) Flood the control queue with agent heartbeats at the same time as sustained client traffic (~200 rps).
3) Observe scheduler moving control tasks into the same priority class as production requests, causing head-of-line blocking and queue build-up.

Observed behavior:
- Scheduler queue depth for the Lodestar pool climbed to 4k+ tasks.
- Worker thread saturation and slow KV cache lookups under pressure.
- Autoscaler did not immediately add capacity due to cooldown tuning tied to CPU instead of queue length.

Expected behavior:
- Edge heartbeats should be rate-limited and handled on a separate low-priority path.
- Autoscaler should consider queue backlog metrics for dedicated pools.

Immediate mitigation applied:
- At 20:22 UTC operations temporarily disabled control_queue processing for the Lodestar pool (configuration toggle).
- At 20:34 UTC we applied a short-term autoscaler override to scale +30% capacity across Lodestar GPUS.
- At 21:40 UTC normal request latency returned to baseline; streaming truncation incidents dropped to zero.

Notes: customer SDKs using exponential-retry patterns contributed to billing amplification; we coordinated with Lodestar to throttle client retries while incident mitigations were active.

investigation_notes: T1: Queue metrics indicated sustained backlog isolated to Lodestar dedicated pool; other tenants unaffected.
T2: Traffic capture showed >10k heartbeats/min from 6 Lodestar edge agents; median heartbeat interval 1s vs expected 30s.
T3: Scheduler configuration had a mapping bug where control tasks were not marked as low-priority when control_queue=true was set by tenant policy.
T4: Autoscaler cooldown was tied to CPU utilization and ignored backlog length for dedicated pools; queue-based scaling rule missing for dedicated tenants.
T5: Client SDK exponential retries increased request volume during the incident window, compounding queue growth and billing impact.
resolution_notes: 1) Immediate: disabled control_queue processing for Lodestar pool (temporary config toggle) to unblock production traffic.
2) Autoscaler override: forced +30% capacity while root cause was mitigated.
3) Long-term: merged PRs to ensure control-heartbeat tasks are routed to a separate low-priority executor path (see related PRs).
4) Billing: approved 15% credit for Lodestar for the affected window; finance will apply credit on next invoice.
5) Customer communication: provided timeline, technical root cause, and recommended SDK/config changes.

Create a tenant onboarding checklist entry documenting recommended edge-agent heartbeat defaults and validation (owner: solutions eng, ETA: 2026-03-10).
Improve billing telemetry to flag unusual token deltas correlated with retry amplification (owner: billing team, ETA: 2026-04-01).
Run a chaos test to simulate control-heartbeat storms in staging and validate separate-path handling (owner: reliability, scheduled: 2026-03-22).

Lodestar accepted a 15% credit for the affected billing window and committed to the recommended edge-agent config change. We apologized for the outage and documented the steps taken to prevent recurrence. Follow-up meeting scheduled for 2026-03-09 to review preventative measures.
